chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf and al-Hasan ibn Ali, all from Ali, from Fadala, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Salama Abu Hafs, from Abu Abdillah, from his father, upon them be peace:

That a man came to Ali (peace be upon him) and had never performed Hajj, so he said: 'I used to have abundant wealth but I neglected Hajj until I grew old.' He said: 'Can you perform Hajj?' He said: 'No.' So Ali (peace be upon him) said to him: 'If you wish, equip a man and then send him to perform Hajj on your behalf.'
ai.seo_question: How does one perform Hajj if they are too old or unable to travel themselves?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights Imam Ali’s (peace be upon him) practical application of *Hajj al-Ni'ab* (proxy pilgrimage), specifically addressing the case of an elderly man who possessed the financial means but lacked the physical capacity to perform Hajj personally. It underscores the Shia juristic consensus that the obligation of Hajj can be fulfilled by a proxy when the individual is unable to travel due to age or infirmity, provided they have the resources to equip the proxy. This incident serves as a foundational precedent for the legal mechanism of delegating religious duties in cases of incapacity.
